articles.headline: Bishops in the City (notice)
articles.summary: Rev. Bishop A. W. Wayman and Bishop Campbell, D.D., are in our city, both looking remarkably well. Bishop Campbell expects to leave for the South this week.

articles.headline: Personal -- Mrs. Francis Watkins Harper in the city (notice)
articles.summary: The celebrated American lecturess, Mrs. Francis Watkins Harper, is in our city. She has just returned from a long but successful tour to the South; the press says no lecturer of either sex has been more successful. Efforts will be made to have her lecture at Liberty Hall.

articles.headline: A Wedding
articles.summary: Marriage of Mr. Matthew Bartholomew, of Pittsburg, Pa., and Miss Mary Wolff, of this city, on Thursday the 26th ult., at the residence of Mrs. Wilkins, performed by Rev. William Alston.

articles.headline: Concert at Cherry Street Baptist Church
articles.summary: The celebrated concert announced some time ago was successfully given at the Cherry Street Baptist Church on the 26th ult. The house was filled by both white and colored people to witness the dedicatory services of a new organ built by Mr. Carter, a colored man, and to hear Miss Greenfield (the Black Swan), Mrs. Brown the opera singer, and Mr. Bowers.

articles.headline: Funeral of Henry McKee, of Camden, New Jersey
articles.summary: The funeral of Brother Henry McKee took place at the A.M.E. Church, Camden, N.J. He departed this life Friday the 27th ult. A large number of friends went over from Philadelphia, among whom were Bishops Wayman and Campbell, Revs. Dorrel, Moore, Giles, Smith, Eddy, and ourself; the Masonic Fraternity was also in attendance. The meeting was opened by the pastor, Rev. J. Hamilton; prayer by Rev. Jacob Mitchell; Bishop Campbell read a portion of the 90th Psalm and of Thessalonians; Bishop Wayman made a short address, followed by Rev. William Moore. McKee came to Philadelphia about 1840, professed a hope in 1838, and was an active Steward, Trustee, and Sabbath School Superintendent.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (moneys received)
articles.summary: Moneys acknowledged (toward the $7,025): Baton Rouge, La., N. Banks, $2.50; Oswego, N.Y., S. J. Hollonsworth, per Rev. Wm. M. Johnson, $2.50; Portland, Me., Rev. J. T. Hazlitt, $11.00; Cold Spring, N.J., per J. Rigby, J. F. Batcear, $2.50; Egg Harbor, N.J., Rev. J. S. Leakens, $1.25; Chester, Pa., Rev. J. Young, $6.85; Zion Mission, Philadelphia, Rev. J. Hollon, $1.00; Bristol, Pa., Rev. E. Laws, $6.32; Cleveland, O., Rev. R. A. Johnson, $20.00; Bloomsburg, Pa., Sunday School, $1.50.

articles.headline: Bishop Campbell's Appointments (notice)
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: No preventing Providence, I shall visit and preach at the following places: Richmond, Ind. (Oct. 6); Indianapolis (Bethel and Allen Chapel); Terre Haute; Alton, Ill.; St. Louis, Mo.; Belleville, Ill.; Brooklyn, Ill.; Cairo, Ill. (Oct. 20); Columbus, Ky.; Memphis, Tenn. (Oct. 27). Brethren near Cairo and Memphis desiring my presence may write to Rev. Thos. Strother at Cairo and Rev. Page Tyler at Memphis.

articles.headline: A Mistake (correction)
articles.author: Mrs. Sarah Ann Simmons
articles.summary: A correction regarding the former wife of Mr. Henry Wilson, who departed this life on the 25th ult.: it is stated that Mrs. Harriet Wilson was not in the city at the time of his funeral.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (James Tillman)
articles.author: James Tillman
articles.summary: Information wanted of my two brothers, Jerry Jarman and Charles Moore, and of my sister, Lydia Bell. They were sold from Wm. Corkell's estate into George Co., Md. Any information thankfully received by their brother. Address James Tillman, Bridgewater Post Office, Bucks Co., Pa.

articles.headline: Married (couples of Chester, Cecil Co. and N.J.)
articles.summary: On the 26th of September, by Rev. I. W. Murphy: Mr. Isaac Emery of Chester, Pa., to Miss Lydia Ann Brown of Cecil County, Md.; same day, by the same, Mr. Ebenezer Hall of Chester, Pa., to Miss Keziah Z. Brown of Cecil County, Md. By another minister: (May 29) William Walters to Miss Anne Bond, both of Bridgeton, N.J.; (Aug. 29) Mr. William Bryan to Miss Emma Reed of Greenwich, N.J.; (Sept. 28) Mr. James Pierce to Miss Isabella Len of Bridgeton, N.J.; (Aug. 16) Mr. Edward Smith to Miss Emma Chaplin of Bridgeton, N.J. Couples are of Chester Pa., Cecil Co. Md., and the Bridgeton/Greenwich N.J. circuit; left in description per owner rule on out-of-area names.

articles.headline: R. M. Adger's furniture store (advertisement)
articles.summary: R. M. Adger's New & Second Hand Furniture Store, No. 716 Lombard St., under Liberty Hall; keeps on hand all kinds of furniture to suit housekeepers.

articles.headline: Dr. William Armstrong, drug commission merchant (advertisement)
articles.summary: Dr. William Armstrong, Drug Commission Merchant, dealer in all kinds of foreign and domestic roots, herbs, and barks, No. 31 North Front Street, Philadelphia. Wants 50,000 pounds of various roots and herbs. Placed under the 'Dentists and Herb Doctors' heading, but reads as a wholesale commission house; proprietor's race/affiliation not confirmed, so no person linked.

articles.headline: Drs. Evans & Rettley -- healing rooms removed (notice)
articles.summary: Drs. Evans and Rettley have removed from their parlors at the Ashland House, Arch Street, to No. 815 Chestnut Street (Sept. 27), where they continue to heal the sick of all manner of diseases; also at their Hall, corner Ninth and Spring Garden Streets, where the poor are healed free. References: Mr. John Draper, 869 Darien street, and Mrs. Allen Taylor, 4604 Frankford street. Proprietors' race/affiliation not confirmed; references are Philadelphia addresses but not linked.

articles.headline: Whipper & Purnell, Lumber Merchants (advertisement)
articles.summary: Whipper & Purnell, Lumber Merchants, N.E. Cor. Broad & Noble Sts., Philadelphia; wholesale and retail dealers in Susquehanna Rafted Lumber, White Pine, Ash, Cherry and Oak. Standing ad dated Dec. 22, 1866 (likely already in DB; captured for completeness).

articles.headline: Empire State House boarding (advertisement)
articles.summary: Empire State House, by Widow T. L. Jinnings, Long Branch, New Jersey; board by the month, week, or day on reasonable terms. (Dated June 1867.)
people: proprietor, Empire State House, Long Branch, N.J. (Widow)

articles.headline: A Rare Chance for a First-Class Dentist (notice)
articles.summary: Wanted, a first-class surgical and mechanical dentist to take the office and laboratory of the late Dr. [—] C. Crummill, who for over twenty years occupied the office and carried on the business. The establishment is fully supplied with instruments. Apply to Sarah Mc. C. Crummill, 449 North Third Street, Philadelphia.

articles.headline: The Vice Presidency (letter)
articles.author: M. R. Delany
articles.summary: A letter dated Hilton Head, S.C., Sept. 27, 1867, to Rev. R. L. Perry, editor of the People's Journal, on the question of a colored Vice Presidency arising out of the South Carolina Convention. Delany argues the race is not yet ready for such a position and names older leaders (Pennington, Garnet, Purvis, Vashon, Langston) whose counsel young men sneer at; mentions the 104 colored policemen in his Sub-Bureau District. Signed M. R. Delany. (Major Martin R. Delany is a watched migrations figure; the letter is from South Carolina.)

articles.headline: Preaching at Cherry Street Baptist Church (notice)
articles.summary: To-morrow at 3 o'clock P.M., the Lord permitting, we will preach by request at the Cherry Street Baptist Church, of which Rev. T. D. Miller is pastor.

articles.headline: Rev. B. T. Tanner's New Book (notice)
articles.summary: We are glad to learn that Rev. B. T. Tanner's work will soon be ready for distribution, and hope that all our readers will procure a copy, as it is a good book.

articles.headline: Success -- festival at Wesley church (notice)
articles.summary: The festival at Wesley church was a success. Everything passed off pleasantly, and all the friends in attendance were satisfied. (Plain 'Wesley church' -- which Wesley not specified; flagged.)

articles.headline: Give Him a Call -- Mr. Adger (notice)
articles.summary: Our friend, Mr. Adger, who has rented one of the store-rooms in Liberty Hall, Lombard Street, has on hand a fine assortment of second-hand furniture, which looks almost as good as new, and which he will sell cheap for cash. Give him a call before purchasing elsewhere.
people: furniture dealer, store-room in Liberty Hall, Lombard St.

articles.headline: More Outrages (street-car harassment)
articles.summary: We learn that some of the negro-hating Democrats, emboldened by their recent success, have already commenced to insult and ill-treat the colored ladies and gentlemen who attempt to ride in the Street Cars. One lady would have been injured had not the conductor and some humane passengers interfered. They had better be a little more careful as to whom they insult so grossly. (STREET-CAR topic: harassment of Black riders in the cars after the October 1867 election.)

articles.headline: Defeated (October 1867 Pennsylvania election)
articles.summary: We are compelled to chronicle the fact that the Republican party has been defeated in the late elections. Pennsylvania has gone Democratic. Some weak-kneed Republicans attribute this to the negro question, but the editor argues the Sunday Liquor and Sunday Car questions were the principal causes: the Republican Party is opposed to the sale of liquor on Sunday and to the running of the Sunday Cars, while the Democrats pandered to the low tastes of the vilest part of the population. (October 1867 PA state election / Black-suffrage context.)

articles.headline: Departed -- Andrew Burris and J. B. Smith (deaths)
articles.summary: We regret to learn of the death of Brother Andrew Burris, so well known in our city by both old and young. He left here some months ago to labor in the South; after a short time near New Orleans he was sent to Texas by Rev. John Turner, where he had an attack of yellow fever which caused his death. He leaves a loving wife and daughter. We are also informed of the death, from yellow fever, of Mr. J. B. Smith, a Baptist missionary, in New Orleans, who was well known in Philadelphia and other places.
people: deceased, of Philadelphia (d. yellow fever, Texas)
deceased, Baptist missionary, well known in Philadelphia (d. New Orleans)

articles.headline: Failure -- Bethel church collection (notice)
articles.summary: Bethel church, on last Sunday, made a failure in the collection for the $7,025, taking up only the small sum of $24. Elder Dorrell called for $300 as the proportion of Bethel. Another attempt would be made the following Sunday; the Elder said he would keep the matter before the church until the required $300 was raised.

articles.headline: Acknowledgment (moneys received)
articles.summary: Moneys acknowledged: New York, N.Y., Rev. H. Davis, $6.40; Flushing, L.I., per Rev. E. B. Davis, D. Cisco, $1.25; per Rev. Wm. H. Brown, P. Smith, Cadiz, O., R. McDowell, Mastersville, O., and M. Epps, Smithfield, O., each $2.50; Bordentown, N.J., A. Thompson, 50 cents; Detroit, Mich., Rev. W. S. Lankford, $1.00; Wilmington, Del., E. H. Anderson, $2.00; Port Republic, N.J., per Rev. R. Barney, A. Smith, $2.50; Hagerstown, Md., per Rev. J. Nicholson, C. Bowen and A. Sampson, each $1.25; Trenton, N.J., Rev. Jas. H. A. Johnson, $1.10.

articles.headline: Married (Smyrna, Del. and a West Philadelphia wedding)
articles.summary: At Smyrna, Del., by Rev. H. H. Lewis: (Sept. 23) James Viney to Miss [—] A. Music; (29th ult.) James Thorn to Miss Ann Foster; (Sept. 29) William Carey to Miss Rhoda A. Cooper, formerly of Laurel, Del.; (Oct. 6) Haslen Fullmore to Miss Selene Anderson -- all of Smyrna (out of scope, in description only). ALSO: Oct. 8, 1867, at the residence of Mrs. H. Brown, 3098 Sansom street, West Philadelphia, Pa., by Rev. H. J. Rhodes, Mr. Noah Cook, of North Carolina, to Miss Rachel Jane Green, of Kent Co., Del.
people: wedding held at her residence, 3098 Sansom St., West Philadelphia

articles.headline: Last Sabbath -- editor's visits to Central Presbyterian and Cherry Street Baptist
articles.summary: On last Sabbath we visited Rev. J. B. Reeve's church (Presbyterian) and walked into the Sabbath School, of which Messrs. Davis and Jones are the Superintendents; Brother Reeves called upon us to preach. In the afternoon we visited the Cherry Street Baptist Church, of which Rev. Theodore D. Miller is pastor; we rejoice in the prosperity of Brother Miller and his people, who have lately purchased a new organ.

articles.headline: New Organ -- Bethel church Sabbath School
articles.summary: Bethel church at last has purchased an American Reed Organ for the use of the Sabbath School. A large number of the young ladies and gentlemen contributed one and two dollars each towards paying for it; it cost $180. The Sabbath School, under the management of Mr. William Banton, has increased in numbers until it is one of the finest, if not the largest, schools in the State. Mr. Banton is a very active, energetic superintendent.

articles.headline: To Our Colored Fellow-Citizens (election / suffrage editorial)
articles.summary: On the result of the late elections in this city and State, and in Ohio: the vote exhibited great prejudice against the loyal colored citizens. The editor condemns foreigners deluded by designing demagogues, noting that nearly all the white Irish who keep grog-shops and groceries on Lombard and Shippen Streets voted the Democratic ticket against the interests of the colored people; advises colored people to spend their money with their own race or with loyal white men who favor universal suffrage, and proposes mass meetings to advise on the proper course. 'In union there is strength.'

articles.headline: Lecture -- Mrs. Ellen W. Harper at Liberty Hall
articles.summary: Mrs. Ellen W. Harper's lecture, on last Monday night, at Liberty Hall, was a grand success. At 8 o'clock she was introduced by our friend, Mr. Josiah Wears, of our city, and the renowned lecturess spoke on color and prejudice ('To-day black is one of the most fashionable colors...'). It was one of the best, both logical and practical; she gave our base ball players some advice. Another lecture from Mrs. Harper is expected in a few days.

articles.headline: Superior Ink -- Mr. Warrington (advertisement)
articles.summary: We have tried Mr. Warrington's superior black ink and pronounce it the best we have ever used; it will not corrode. It can be had at retail or wholesale from the manufacturer, at No. 612 Federal Street, Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Philadelphia Churches (survey)
articles.summary: A survey of Philadelphia churches. BETHEL CHURCH: Rev. D. Dorrell, pastor, has been absent on a visit to his family. UNION (ZION) WESLEY CHURCH: Rev. John A. Williams, pastor, has commenced a series of meetings; the house is crowded every night. WESLEY A.M.E. CHURCH: Rev. Geo. A. Boyer, pastor, held their love feast last Tuesday night, Rev. J. Hamilton (pastor of the Camden church) presiding; Brother Boyer is mending. COATES STREET A.M.E. CHURCH: Rev. William Moore, pastor; Brother Simpson, a leading member, is agent for the Recorder. ZION MISSION CHURCH: Rev. J. Hollan, pastor, in good condition. THE BAPTIST CHURCHES: Rev. Theo. D. Miller has charge of the Pearl Street church; Scott's is under Rev. Mr. Underdue; the Shiloh church is without a pastor, Rev. Mr. Leonard having resigned.
people: pastor, Camden church; presided at Wesley love feast (Rev.)
in charge of the Pearl Street Baptist church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Left for Savannah, Ga. -- R. P. Gibbs
articles.summary: Rev. R. P. Gibbs left this city for that point (Savannah, Ga.) on Saturday last. May success attend him. (Migration of a Philadelphia A.M.E. clergyman to the South.)

articles.headline: Memorial resolutions -- A.M.E. Mission Sabbath-school (N.J.)
articles.summary: Resolutions by the teachers of the A.M.E. Mission Sabbath-school (N.J., dated Oct. 8, 1867) on the death of their beloved Superintendent, a co-worker affectionate as a companion and exemplary as a Christian; sympathy extended to his bereaved wife. Committee: Mrs. J. Harris, Mrs. E. Sullivan, Miss C. Leary, Miss A. Collins, Miss M. Tucker, Miss E. Sullivan, J. Harris. J. Dennickson, Secretary. (The deceased Superintendent's name was not legible on the film; the place name is garbled.)

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (moneys received)
articles.summary: Moneys acknowledged: Lewistown, Pa., per S. Molson, J. Barile, $2; Boston, Mass., per Rev. E. T. Williams, Mrs. A. Watkins, $1.25. Per Rev. Theo. Gould, Travelling Agent: Orange, N.J., J. H. Henson and R. Clark, each $2.50; P. Brightwell, $3. Newark, N.J., M. Jones, S. E. King and S. E. Williams, each $3.

articles.headline: Married (a Philadelphia wedding and others)
articles.summary: At Penningtonville, Oct. 10, 1867, by Rev. W. H. Turner, Mr. Levi Johnson to Miss Frances Williams, both of Chester Co. AT PHILADELPHIA, October 10, 1867, by Rev. Jeremiah Young, Mr. Clinton Johnson (of Pennsburg) to Miss Anna M. Hutchinson, of Chester. Also (out of area, description only): Oct. 2, by Rev. J. [--]by, George W. Barner of Sharpsburg, Md., to Mary Catherine Woollard of Berkeley Co., Va.; Oct. 7, a Mr. Dorsey of Baltimore to a Miss Boston of Lancaster Co., Pa.; Oct. 14, a Mr. [--]well Shantle of Petersburg, Va., to Hannah E. Gundy of Delaware.

articles.headline: Died -- William Lee
articles.summary: At Philadelphia, Oct. 8, 1867, William Lee, in the 64th year of his age. Brother Lee suffered about eighteen months under dropsy, asthma and heart disease; he died happy in the love of his Saviour. A kind and affectionate wife and daughter mourn his loss.

articles.headline: Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins returned from Cape May (notice)
articles.summary: The good people of Philadelphia will be rejoiced to learn that Mrs. Hawkins has returned home from Cape May, where she keeps a store during the summer. Her place of business is at 615 Lombard St., where she keeps a large assortment of fall, winter, spring and summer goods. (Her standing 615 Lombard ad is already in the DB.)

articles.headline: The Philadelphia Morning Post (notice)
articles.summary: We have received, by way of exchange, several copies of the Morning Post, published by Mr. McClintock, a staunch friend of ours, and edited by Mr. Stockton, who for two years had been a correspondent for the New York Tribune. A daily of moderate size, well printed. (Publisher/editor appear to be white; not linked.)

articles.headline: Book Notice -- An Apology for African Methodism, by Rev. B. T. Tanner
articles.summary: We have just received a package of copies of this new and eagerly looked-for book, addressed to the Bishops, Elders, Deacons and members of the A.M.E. Church; 468 pages, cloth bound, with original poetry by the author on the last pages. Brother Tanner has shown what colored men can do, collating many facts relative to our Church and people. $1.02 per copy, of the author or at our Book Store, No. 631 Pine St., Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Union A.M.E. Church -- quarterly meeting held (report)
articles.summary: On last Sabbath the congregation of Union A.M.E. Church held its Quarterly Meeting. Preaching in the morning by Rev. J. Hamilton; in the afternoon by Rev. Deacon Dorrell, of Bethel; and at night by Rev. Wm. Moore. (Report of the meeting announced Oct. 19 for Oct. 20.)

articles.headline: Zion Wesley Church -- protracted meeting (notice)
articles.summary: At Zion Wesley Church, of which Rev. John A. Williams is pastor, the protracted meeting is still going on; several have been converted. We preached on last Monday night to a crowded house, and twenty-five came forward and knelt at the anxious bench.

articles.headline: St. Thomas' Church -- Rev. William Alston to resign (notice)
articles.summary: We have heard that the Rev. William Alston is about to resign the pastoral care of St. Thomas' Church. We will greatly regret to lose him from our city; we have ever been on the best terms with Mr. Alston, and believe he was loved by all who knew him.

articles.headline: Last Sabbath -- visit to the West Philadelphia A.M.E. Church
articles.summary: On last Sabbath, in company with the Rev. Stephen Smith, we visited the West Philadelphia A.M.E. Church, of which Rev. J. H. Rhodes is pastor, on the occasion of its quarterly meeting. We repaired to the residence of the Rev. Richard Henry, Deacon of the church, and the pastor desired us to preach. The service was opened by Brother Smith, who afterward lifted a collection of over $20 to assist in paying for the new church. We then went to Bethel church and heard an excellent discourse from the Rev. Watkins, and at night preached in the same church to a large congregation.
people: accompanied; opened service and lifted collection (Rev.)

articles.headline: Dr. Rosell's Success as Medical Professor (notice)
articles.summary: This celebrated colored physician, who passed a successful medical examination at one of the German Colleges of Surgeons in Europe, has again added to his medical celebrity by his complete success in a recent cure. We enlist the patronage of the public to the practice of Dr. Rosell's.

articles.headline: Stabbing with a Knife (notice)
articles.summary: A few days since the elder son of Mr. O'Donnell of this city was stabbed by another young man who inflicted three severe wounds near the heart; had it not been for the timely call of a surgeon, Dr. Rosell's, he would have succumbed. We advise our young men to beware how they use any dangerous weapon.

articles.headline: African Union Church committee reply regarding Samuel P. Smith (notice)
articles.summary: A committee appointed by our Conference replies to a notice published and signed by Samuel P. Smith and others, in which Smith claims to be the Elder of the African Union Church and claims all churches built for and deeded to the A.U. Church. The committee states that Samuel P. Smith is not a member of their connection, having been expelled on the 16th of June of this year for an immoral crime; his character has been very bad; at Chester, Delaware county, his suit for damages to his character returned a verdict of six cents. The other persons named never were members. They warn that further such notices may bring the penalty of the law. Signed: Rt. Rev. Benjamin Jefferson; Rev. Hazar Moor; Rev. James L. Smith; Daniel D. Morgan (his mark); Geo. W. Bostwick, Secretary.
people: committee; bishop, African Union Church (Rt. Rev.)
expelled from the African Union connection (subject)

articles.headline: Arrivals at Mrs. Huskerson's Boarding House, New York (notice)
articles.summary: Arrivals at Mrs. Huskerson's Boarding House, 21 Green street, New York (Oct. 21, 1867): Dr. A. Abbott, Toronto; Mrs. Thomas Dorsey and daughter, Philadelphia; John R. Kennedy, Philadelphia; C. L. Randanie, Boston; Thomas S. Boston; a Washington D.C. guest; Rev. Mr. Adams, Charleston, S.C.; John Sharp, Liberia; Mrs. Elizabeth Keckley, Washington, D.C.; William E. Matthews, Baltimore; Mr. E. Lawrence, New York; Mrs. Elizabeth T. Greenfield and Troupe, Philadelphia; H. Miller, California; J. H. Ranney, Georgetown, S.C.; Miss Frances Rollin, Charleston, S.C. (The Philadelphians Mrs. Thomas Dorsey and John R. Kennedy are linked; Mrs. Elizabeth T. Greenfield = the Black Swan, kept text-only per owner ruling; the rest are out of town.)

articles.headline: Died -- Edward Doyer
articles.summary: Edward Doyer departed this life on the 6th instant, in Port Republic, N.J., being about 80 years of age. He is said to have been a good man and a friend to the cause. His funeral sermon was preached by Rev. Richard Harris, his pastor, on the 13th inst.
people: deceased (d. Oct. 6, 1867, Port Republic, N.J., age ~80)

articles.headline: Third Letter to Our Colored Fellow-Citizens (election / suffrage editorial)
articles.summary: Third in the editorial series addressing colored citizens after the October elections: on the generous efforts of right-minded politicians to wipe away the opprobrium that has rendered American institutions ridiculous in the eyes of civilized Christendom, and the duty of colored men of well-constituted minds to dispute, with warmth and perspicuity, the rationality of anti-constitutional procedure. 'With justice on our side, let us never be weary till we have every vestige of our stolen rights restored to us.' (Continues the Oct. 19 'To Our Colored Fellow-Citizens' editorial.)

articles.headline: Memorial resolutions -- Andrew Burris, Sabbath School Superintendent
articles.summary: Resolutions by the teachers of the A.M.E. Church Sabbath School on the death of their beloved brother Andrew Burris, Superintendent of their Sabbath School (with which he was long and intimately connected), bearing testimony to the warmth of his heart and the energy of his spirit in all his labors, and extending Christian condolence to the bereaved family. (Andrew Burris was reported dead of yellow fever in Texas in the Oct. 12 issue; this memorial confirms he was superintendent of a Philadelphia A.M.E. Sabbath School.)
people: deceased; Superintendent of the A.M.E. Sabbath School

articles.headline: Memorial resolutions -- Landon G. Clark (Lincoln University)
articles.summary: At a prayer meeting of the students of Lincoln University (Oct. 8th, 1867), preamble and resolutions on the death of Landon G. Clark, of Reading, Pa., a student, beloved and respected for his exemplary character; deep sympathy with his aged grandparent and his relatives. Committee: W. L. Johnson, J. S. Thompson, A. H. Grimke, H. H. Fay, Wm. R. Templeton.
people: deceased; student, Lincoln University (of Reading, Pa.)

articles.headline: Lodging -- Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller (notice)
articles.summary: Two or three respectable young men can find good and permanent lodging, on reasonable terms, by applying to Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller, 208 Quince St., below Walnut. (Theo. Doughty Miller = the Rev. T. D. / Theodore D. Miller, pastor of the Cherry Street Baptist / Pearl Street church.)

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Daniel McCullom)
articles.author: Daniel McCullom
articles.summary: Information wanted of my brother, James Thomas, of North Carolina, formerly of Washington, D.C.; in 1863 I left him in Newbern, North Carolina, working in the service of the Government. Also of Sam Demont, whom I left in Washington, D.C. Address Daniel McCullom, 258 Currant Alley, Phila. (Ministers in Newbern asked to read this to their congregations.)
people: brother sought (of North Carolina, formerly Washington, D.C.)

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (moneys received)
articles.summary: Moneys acknowledged: Pennington, N.J., per Rev. W. Thompson, P. Light, $2.50; Atchison, Kansas, Rev. J. P. Jordan, $2.25; Baltimore, Md., per R. W. Schureman, S. Brown, 85 cts.; Cadiz, Ohio, per Rev. W. H. Brown, M. J. Joiner, $1.22, N. A. Clark and A. Mason each $2.50, for books $8.00; New York, Rev. H. Davis, $6.40; Princeton, New Jersey, Rev. J. H. A. Johnson, $1.20. A correction notes Rev. J. W. Davis [reading uncertain] should have been credited $5.20, not $2.50.

articles.headline: Married (Chester, Pa. and New York)
articles.summary: On September 19th, 1867, at Chester, Pa., by Rev. W. Murphy, Mr. John H. Ridgeley, of Chester, to Mrs. Margaret Lucas, of Frederick City, Md.; same day, by the same, Mr. Levi Cooper to Miss Mary Hailon, all of Chester. Also (out of scope, description only): Oct. 10, in New York, by Rev. Henry Davis, Mr. Henry J. Johnson to Miss Sarah Allen; Oct. 24, same place, by the same, Mr. Sutton Caesar Hammond to Miss Ann Maria Risen.

events.name: West Philadelphia Circuit -- quarterly meetings
events.location: Norristown, West Philadelphia, and Germantown, Pa.
events.description: Quarterly meetings of the West Philadelphia Circuit: Norristown, Pa., Sunday October 13th, 1867; West Philadelphia, Sunday Oct. 20th; Germantown, Sunday Oct. 27th. A pressing invitation extended to friends of Christianity, particularly at West Philadelphia. Signed by the minister in charge, Rev. H. J. Rhodes (surname confirmed from the Oct. 12 marriage notice he officiated). Notice ran Oct. 5 and Oct. 12.

events.name: Frankford quarterly meeting
events.description: Quarterly Meeting at Frankford, Pa., on Sabbath October 6th; preaching at 11 A.M., 6 and 7.30 P.M., by Rev. Wm. Moore and others. Daniel P. Seaton, Pastor.

events.name: Wesley (Hurst Street / Little Wesley) A.M.E. quarterly meeting
events.location: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly Meeting at Wesley A.M.E. church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia, on Sabbath, October 13th. Pastor Rev. Geo. A. Boyer (the Oct. 19 'Philadelphia Churches' survey names 'Rev. Geo. A. Boyer' pastor of Wesley A.M.E. Church; the garbled 'Geo. E. Burks' reading of the Oct. 5 and Oct. 12 signatures is corrected to Boyer). Hurst Street Wesley = Little Wesley (A.M.E.) per owner ruling. Notice ran Oct. 5 and Oct. 12.

events.name: Sheba Lodge, Juvenile I.O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria
events.location: Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Directory listing. Sheba Lodge, Juvenile I.O. of Good Samaritans and D. of Samaria, meets the 2d Thursday of each month at 3 o'clock P.M. at Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street. Officers: A. Cropper and S. Young (each listed 'P.G.').

events.name: Sumner and Wilson Lodge, No. 8, I.O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria
events.location: Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Directory listing. Sumner and Wilson Lodge, No. 8, I.O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria, meets the second and fourth Thursdays of each month at Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street, Philadelphia, at 8 o'clock. No officers named in this listing.

events.name: Bensalem / Bristol Circuit -- quarterly meetings
events.location: Bensalem, Harrisburg Mill, and Bristol, Pa.
events.description: The Second Quarterly Meeting will be held at Bensalem, Pa., Oct. 12 and 13; Quarterly Conference on the 12th at 1 o'clock; on the 19th and 20th at Harrisburg Mill [reading uncertain]; and at Bristol on the 26th and 27th. Signed D. P. Seaton, Elder-in-Charge, and E. Laws, Deacon.

events.name: Bethel Church quarterly meeting
events.description: A Quarterly Meeting will be held at the Bethel Church, Oct. 27. Preaching at 10 o'clock by Rev. D. P. Seaton; at 3 o'clock by Rev. William Moore; and at 7.30 by Rev. J. B. Hamilton. Love feast, Monday evening the 28th. Signed D. Dorrell, Pastor. (The p2 'Failure' item the same week also ties 'Elder Dorrell' to Bethel's $300 collection quota -- see flags re the Bethel pastor.)

events.name: Sheba Lodge No. 1 (Juvenile I.O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria) -- Fifth Grand Anniversary
events.location: Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street, Philadelphia
events.description: The Fifth Grand Anniversary of Sheba Lodge No. 1, I.O. of G.S. and Daughters of Samaria of Juveniles, Oct. 28 at 8 P.M., Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street. A Bible to be presented by Rev. T. D. Miller and received by Rev. Stephen Smith, Treasurer of said Lodge. Rev. J. Hamilton, Rev. E. Weaver, and Rev. D. P. Seaton to address the audience. Tickets 25 cents, children 10 cents, of the Committee: A. Cropper (P.G.), S. Young (P.G.), O. Stokes (R.G.), and at the door.
attendees: treasurer of the Lodge; to receive the Bible (Rev.)

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church (Coates St. below Fifth) -- quarterly meeting
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church, Coates Street below Fifth, Philadelphia
events.description: A Quarterly Meeting at the Union A.M.E. Church, Coates St. below Fifth, Sunday Oct. 20. Preaching at 10 A.M. by Rev. J. B. Hamilton; 3 P.M., Rev. D. Dorrell; 7.30 P.M., Rev. Wm. Moore. Love Feast Monday evening, Oct. 21.

events.name: Media / Thornbury / West Chester -- quarterly meetings
events.location: Media, Thornbury, and West Chester, Pa.
events.description: Quarterly meetings at Media on the 26th inst., Thornbury on the 2d and 3d of November, and West Chester on the 9th and 10th of November, 1867. Signed John C. [surname garbled], Minister-in-charge.

events.name: Preachers' Association of the Philadelphia Conference -- meeting at Bethel
events.description: All members of the Preachers' Association of the Philadelphia Conference requested to attend their meeting at Bethel Church, Tuesday the 22d inst., at 10 A.M.; business of importance. By order of the President, Wm. Moore. D. P. Seaton, Secretary.

events.name: Central Presbyterian Church -- Board of Trustees election
events.location: Central Presbyterian Church, Lombard street below Ninth, Philadelphia
events.description: At an election held October 14th, 1867, the following gentlemen were elected for the ensuing year for the Board of Trustees of the Central Presbyterian Church (Rev. J. B. Reeve's church), Lombard street below Ninth, Philadelphia: W. D. Lawson [surname uncertain], James W. Brown, James A. Potter, Joseph H. Young, Addison Foster, W. C. Dixon, Samuel H. Barrett, Isaiah Wilson, and John McKee.

events.name: Snowhill, N.J. -- cornerstone of the new A.M.E. Church
events.description: The corner-stone of the new A.M.E. Church at Snowhill, N.J., will be laid on Sunday, Nov. 3d, by Rev. Stephen Smith and Rev. J. B. Hamilton. Persons leaving Philadelphia will take the Vine street cars and get their tickets for Haddonfield, N.J. Signed J. W. Stevenson, Minister-in-Charge.

events.name: Penningtonville Circuit -- quarterly meetings
events.description: Quarterly meetings will be held on the Penningtonville Circuit, Black Rock, in October. Signed W. H. Turner, Pastor.

events.name: Shiloh Union Lodge No. 12 (I.O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria) -- organized at Springfield, Pa.
events.description: Certifies that a Lodge of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria was organized at Springfield, Pa., working under the jurisdiction of the Grand Lodge No. 2 for Pennsylvania and Delaware, on October 24th, 1867, under the title of Shiloh Union Lodge, No. 12. Officers elected (as printed; several surnames uncertain on the film): Noah Stunt, P.[?]; Maria Miller, P.D.; Edward Brown, C.; Rebecca Knead, P.D.; Thomas Knowl, R.C.; Rebecca Brown, F.C.; Wm. Muller, V.C.; Susan Lockwood, D.P. Haver H. Gilbert, Grand Chief. James Gottomno and A. Cropper, District Deputies.

events.name: Penningtonville A.M.E. Church -- special meeting
events.location: A.M.E. Church, Penningtonville, Chester County, Pa.
events.description: A special meeting will be held in the A.M.E. church at Penningtonville, Chester County, Pa., commencing November 9th and closing November 11th. Signed Wm. H. Turner, Pastor.
